Morning always arrives like a soft announcement—no trumpets, just a gradual turning of the world from dim to definite. I like that about it. At first the windows look almost imaginary, as if the light hasn’t decided whether it’s real yet. Then, one small detail at a time, everything commits: the dust in the air becomes visible, the floorboards take on their familiar grain, and the horizon sharpens into something I can trust.

I used to think time was a straight line, a hallway with doors you either walked through or missed. Lately I’ve been feeling it more like weather. Some days are clear and bright and easy to name. Other days roll in heavy and gray, and you can’t quite tell whether they’ll lift or stay. Still, the clouds move. Even when nothing changes on the surface, the atmosphere keeps rearranging itself.

There are moments I cling to—steam curling from a mug, a song leaking through a neighbor’s open window, the brief hush before a bus pulls up. They feel small, but maybe that’s the point. Life doesn’t always shout. Sometimes it only taps your shoulder with something ordinary, asking you to notice.

And when I notice—truly notice—I feel less like I’m passing through my own days and more like I’m in them.
